core.big_idea: God sent Jesus into the world as promised.

passages.reading_note: Read the central passage with attention to context and age-appropriate scope.

core.metanarrative_position: Gospel: the promised Messiah enters history in humility.

claims.statement: Jesus was born in Bethlehem during the time of Caesar Augustus.
An angel announced good news of a Savior, Christ the Lord.
The shepherds went to see the child and then praised God.
Luke presents Jesus’ birth as good news with significance for God’s people.

core.interpretation_skill: Identify genre and context, separate direct observation from synthesis or inference, and connect the passage to the whole-Bible story without forced symbolism.

learning.foundation_objective: Explain in age-appropriate language that god sent Jesus into the world as promised.
learning.extension_objective: Locate the lesson in the whole-Bible story and distinguish direct textual claims from later synthesis or application.
know: God sent Jesus into the world as promised.
The lesson belongs within the wider biblical storyline.
understand: Biblical meaning depends on context and genre.
Application should follow what the text supports rather than replace it.
practise: Use one observation question before giving an interpretation.
Retell the birth story in five steps and thank God for sending Jesus.
become: A learner who reads Scripture carefully and responds with trust, wisdom, and love.
success_evidence: Student can retell or summarize the central passage.
Student can state the big idea without adding unsupported details.
Student can name one appropriate response.

zero_prep_card.objective: Explain in age-appropriate language that god sent Jesus into the world as promised.
zero_prep_card.opening: Ask: What do you notice first in this passage, before we explain what it means?
say: Jesus was born in Bethlehem during the time of Caesar Augustus.
An angel announced good news of a Savior, Christ the Lord.
God sent Jesus into the world as promised.
We will separate what the passage says from what we infer or apply.
ask: What happens or is said in the passage?
What does this show about God, people, or the biblical story?
Which statement is directly in the text?
What is one careful response for us?
zero_prep_card.do: Complete the Good News Sequence activity.
zero_prep_card.close: Pray using one truth from the passage and one faithful response.

preparation.passage_context: Gospel: the promised Messiah enters history in humility.
text_observations: Jesus was born in Bethlehem during the time of Caesar Augustus.
An angel announced good news of a Savior, Christ the Lord.
The shepherds went to see the child and then praised God.
Luke presents Jesus’ birth as good news with significance for God’s people.
interpretation_notes: Start with the principal passage before moving to supporting texts.
Keep genre and original audience visible.
Label synthesis, historical context, and application rather than presenting them as quotations.
theological_guardrails: Do not add traditional details that Luke does not state as though they were in the passage.
Do not reduce the lesson to sentimentality; keep Jesus’ identity central.
Avoid pressuring children to perform emotion or public devotion.

likely_questions.question: Were there three wise men at the stable?
likely_questions.purpose: Matthew mentions magi but does not state there were three or place them in Luke’s shepherd scene.

likely_questions.question: Why was Jesus born in such a simple place?
likely_questions.purpose: Luke shows the Savior entering ordinary human life without worldly status.

accessibility.plain_language_rule: Prefer short sentences, define unfamiliar biblical terms, and do not require independent reading beyond the segment.
neurodiversity_supports: Give instructions one step at a time.
Allow verbal, written, or pointing responses.
Preview transitions and allow a pass option.
sensory_notes: No activity requires loud sound, forced touch, or competitive speed.
non_reader_support: Teacher or parent may read aloud.
Use sequence cards, symbols, or oral responses.

do_not_ask: Do not require disclosure of private family circumstances.
Do not require public confession or religious decision.
Do not use physical touch without consent.
safeguarding.teacher_response: If a child discloses harm, danger, abuse, severe distress, or unmet basic needs, follow the congregation safeguarding process rather than trying to investigate in class.

editorial.scripture_text_policy: Store references and editorial summaries; add licensed translation text only after permissions are confirmed.
